title: Evidence register
lede: Which organizations actually move student outcomes, and which are still finding out. This is a register, not a ranking: there is no outcome measure comparable across organizations, so entries are grouped by the strength of the evidence behind them and every effect size is quoted with the study that produced it. The second lane holds work that is genuinely new, where results are not in yet.

blocks.title: The register: nonprofits with rigorous evidence
blocks.subtitle: Organizations whose flagship program has been evaluated in a randomized trial. Effect sizes are in standard deviations (SD) and are quoted with the study that produced them; they are not comparable across different outcomes and populations.

cells: Ampact (Reading Corps)
AmeriCorps literacy tutors embedded in K-3 classrooms, working with 15 to 18 students for 20 minutes each a day
Two randomized studies with 798 students; average effect +0.36 SD, reaching +0.74 on letter-sound fluency in the Minnesota trial
Chapter One
Part-time tutors push into kindergarten classrooms for 5 to 10 minute bursts during reading blocks, rather than pulling students out
Two randomized studies with 1,009 students; average effect +0.23 SD, and +0.31 on the district reading level assessment in the larger trial
BARR Center
A ninth-grade whole-school model built on teacher teams, deliberate relationship building and weekly review of student data
Randomized trial across 11 high schools in five states; +0.21 SD on grades and course failure and +0.17 on relationships, but no gain on NWEA reading or math
Saga Education
In-school math tutoring for ninth and tenth graders, at least three times a week, at ratios between one to two and one to four
Three randomized trials with 5,396 students; average effect +0.14 SD, with per-study effects of +0.09, +0.14 and +0.19 for students assigned to tutoring
Reading Partners
Community volunteers tutor students in grades 2 to 5 one-to-one, twice a week, in a dedicated reading center inside the school
One large randomized trial by MDRC with 1,166 students; effect +0.10 SD on comprehension, against a control group that mostly received other literacy support
Khan Academy
Free online practice, plus Khanmigo, an AI tutor configured to coach a student through a problem rather than hand over the answer
Two-year cluster randomized trial in 18 Tennessee middle schools; +1.3 national percentile ranks per term, roughly 0.06 to 0.08 SD a year, similar to Khan practice without the AI

blocks.title: The watch lane: new approaches, results pending
blocks.subtitle: Work that is deliberately unproven. Each entry names the evidence that would settle it, so a reader can tell promise from proof.

cells: Accelerate and the Oklahoma State Department of Education
A $13.76 million federal grant funds high-impact literacy tutoring for about 6,000 K-5 students reading below benchmark, across urban and rural districts
A multi-arm randomized trial comparing virtual against in-person delivery, group size and dosage, with cost analysis built in and Mathematica evaluating
Accelerate's tutoring grants
Up to $250,000 each for Carnegie Learning, Chapter One, Math-A-Matics Tutoring and Tutored by Teachers to run tutoring inside the school day
Which students benefit most, in which subjects and grades, and whether group size or session length is what drives the effect
Accelerate's classroom technology grants
Eight organizations including the nonprofit Quill.org and Third Space Learning, each paired with an independent research partner and given $150,000 to $200,000
Whether early student progress shows up in achievement, and what quality standards should govern classroom AI
Khan Academy's engagement problem
The AI tutor only works when students open it: the median student used it on a third of practice days and in 17% of sessions after making a mistake
Designs that raise voluntary use without raising cost, since the trial's effects tracked usage rather than the technology itself
Air Reading
Live virtual literacy tutoring for grades 1 to 6, already rated Strong, now being deployed at state scale as part of the Oklahoma study
Whether a Strong rating survives state-scale delivery, and what it costs per student next to in-person tutoring

items.headline: The tiers come from federal law, not from us.
items.detail: The Every Student Succeeds Act defines four tiers: strong evidence from a randomized trial, moderate from a quasi-experiment, promising from a correlational study with controls, and a fourth tier that asks only for a logic model. Interventions paid for with Title I school improvement money must reach Tiers 1 to 3.

items.headline: There is no honest way to rank these organizations.
items.detail: Effect sizes come from different outcomes, grade bands and populations, so +0.36 on letter-sound fluency in kindergarten is not better or worse than +0.14 on a high school math test. Sorting by tier and reading the study is the only defensible comparison.

items.headline: A rating describes a program, not an organization.
items.detail: Evidence for ESSA rates a named program in a named category. BARR alone holds Strong ratings in reading, math, attendance and social-emotional learning, while an organization with one rated program may run several unrated ones.

items.headline: Absence of a rating is not evidence of absence.
items.detail: Khan Academy has a two-year randomized trial behind it but no ESSA rating, because nobody has submitted it. Newer and smaller organizations are systematically underrepresented in every clearinghouse.

items.label: Evidence for ESSA standards last revised
items.note: Run by the Center for Research and Reform in Education at Johns Hopkins with a technical work group; programs are submitted for review.

items.label: Attendance programs with an ESSA rating
items.note: The thinnest evidence base of any category, against the largest problem: 22.6% of students were chronically absent in 2024-25.

items.label: Largest attendance trial in the catalog
items.note: Two randomized trials of mailed absence reports to parents, in Philadelphia and a California county. Run by EveryDay Intervention, whose corporate form this register does not verify.

items.label: The federal clearinghouse
items.note: The What Works Clearinghouse remains the federal evidence review, but the Institute of Education Sciences published a restructuring strategy in February 2026 amid the department's wider reorganization.

items.label: Evidence for ESSA
items.note: Rates named PK-12 programs against the ESSA tiers across six categories, with the underlying studies described on each program page.

items.label: What Works Clearinghouse
items.note: The Institute of Education Sciences review, running since 2002, reporting effect sizes and improvement indices.

items.label: National Student Support Accelerator
items.note: Tutoring-specific standards, a provider directory and the research base behind high-impact tutoring.

items.label: Accelerate
items.note: Funds tutoring and classroom technology, pairs each grantee with an independent evaluator, and publishes what the trials find.

items.label: ESSA itself
items.note: Section 8101(21)(A) is where the four tiers are defined and where the funding requirement comes from.
